question: What gives the counters of the units under a selected one their ring.

addresses.name: CUnit_SetRingBelow
addresses.comment: **Gives every unit of a list, and every unit under any of them, one ring.** For each unit of the list that is not itself selected (the byte at +4), the two counters of its avatar (+0x164, then +0x140 and +0x13C) get CCounterObject::SetSelection(state); then the same for its own list of units (+0x1E4) where that has any (+0x1EC). CUnit::OnSelected calls it with 3 - the counter type's color2 - and CUnit::OnDeselected with 0. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: Read end to end, 0x5C0580..0x5C05EA: the loop, the test of [unit+4], the two calls through slot 23 with the first argument, the recursion on unit+0x1E4 behind the test of +0x1EC. Bare `ret`, two stack arguments cleaned by the caller (`add esp, 8` at 0x5C0891).

addresses.name: CUnit::OnSelected
addresses.comment: Slot 4, one body for CUnit, CArmy, CNavy and CAir: what a unit does when it becomes selected. Among it: **its own two counters get ring 1, white, and CUnit_SetRingBelow(3, its units) gives every unit under it the counter type's color2.** CInGameIdler::ShowSelection afterwards makes the selected unit's own ring 2, color1, where an AI commands it. Read for the rings only; the rest - its arrow, its avatar, the sound - was not. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: 0x5C0857..0x5C0891: `push 1` before each of the two calls through slot 23 of [avatar+0x140] and [avatar+0x13C], then `lea eax,[ebx+0x1e4]; push eax; push 3; call 0x5c0580`. `ret 4`.

addresses.name: CUnit::OnDeselected
addresses.comment: Slot 5, one body for CUnit, CArmy, CNavy and CAir: what a unit does when it is selected no longer. Frees its arrow (keeping its counter at +0x18C), destroys the object at +0x168, **sets its own two counters' ring to 0 and CUnit_SetRingBelow(0, its units)**, and clears the province's +0x2E8. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: Read end to end: CUnit::FreeArrow on +0x188, CGraphics::DestroyVisibleObject on +0x168, the two calls through slot 23 with 0, the call of 0x5C0580 with 0 and unit+0x1E4. Bare `ret`.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::ShowSelection
addresses.comment: Slot 32. Clears what the last selection drew on the map - the markers of an AI's objectives, the arrows - and, for a unit of the player's, **gives its two counters their ring: 1, white, or 2, the counter type's color1, where an AI agent commands the unit or one above it**; then, for an AI-commanded unit, the objective markers and the AutomationArrow of its plan. Read as far as the ring; the name is ours. The ring 3 of the units under a selected one is not set here but by CUnit::OnSelected, through CUnit_SetRingBelow. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: 0x668AD1..0x668B29 and 0x66925B..0x66927B: the walk of +0x198 up +0x1E0, then `push 2` before both calls through slot 23 where an agent was found and `push 1` where none was. `ret 4`.
addresses.revises: the comment's last sentence: it said no caller passing 3 was found, and the caller is now recorded
